--- title: "Visualizations" vignette: > %\VignetteIndexEntry{Visualizations} %\VignetteEngine{quarto::html} %\VignetteEncoding{UTF-8} --- Interactive exemplars for the three chart families the project uses: **time series**, **2D**, and **3D**. Each reads a pipeline target, so the input → chart lineage is explicit. The default stack is R htmlwidgets (`plotly`, `ggiraph`); Observable JS is reserved for bespoke explorables (a later addition). ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} picks <- tar_read(picks) |> filter(year >= 2013, !is.na(height), !is.na(weight), !is.na(overall)) ``` ::: ## Time series — drafts per year ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} viz_drafts_by_season(tar_read(model_table)) ``` ::: {#fig-timeseries .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## 2D — draft capital vs. physicals (hover for player) Each point is a drafted player; hover for the name. Color encodes draft round. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} viz_scatter_2d( dplyr::slice_sample(picks, n = min(1500, nrow(picks))), x = weight, y = height, tooltip = name, color = round ) ``` ::: {#fig-2d .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## 3D — height × weight × overall pick ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} viz_scatter_3d( picks, x = "height", y = "weight", z = "overall", color = "round" ) ``` ::: {#fig-3d .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## NFL outcomes — how long drafted players last Each point is a drafted player bridged to nflverse (decision 0014), placed by draft round against the number of distinct **seasons they spent on an NFL roster** — the project's primary longevity measure. The **#1 overall picks** are highlighted against the rest of the field; the grey bar marks each round's median. Hover for the player. Recent draft classes are still active, so their counts are **right-censored** lower bounds. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} viz_nfl_roster_seasons_by_round(tar_read(picks_nfl), tar_read(nfl_rosters)) ``` ::: {#fig-nfl-longevity .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ## Career length — how long is a college career? Each player's career is summarized from the **roster backbone** — distinct seasons on a roster per athlete id, including seasons with no stat line. The shape of this distribution is the baseline every other career question is read against: most careers are short, so a fifth or sixth season is already a distinct population, and how long a player stayed in college plausibly shapes both their development and their draft odds. Gap seasons (years absent between first and last appearance) are also recorded here — they are the raw material for the injury-shaped-gap analysis below. Hover a bar for the player count. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} viz_career_length(tar_read(roster)) ``` ::: {#fig-career-length .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note} A long career is not always continuous: a fifth or sixth season can be a redshirt year, a medical hardship, or a COVID-era extension, and the roster grain cannot separate them. The next section formalizes what *can* be inferred about redshirts from this data — approximately, and with an explicit confound. ::: ## Redshirts — what the data can and cannot say A **redshirt** is an NCAA eligibility designation: a player spends a season on a roster **without competing in it**, and that season does not count against their four seasons of eligibility — they effectively gain a fifth (sometimes sixth) year. Since 2018 a redshirted player may still appear in up to four games without burning the redshirt, so "played a little" and "redshirted" are no longer mutually exclusive. No feed in this project labels who redshirted, so it must be **inferred** — approximately — from two signals: 1. **Stat-gap shape** — a roster season with **no stat line that the player returned from**. Here a *stat line* means any recorded season statistic for that player-season in the `player_stats` table — a pass attempt, a tackle, a reception, anything. Having **no** stat line is our best available proxy for "did not compete". The "returned from" guard matters: a final-year absence is just as likely an injury or an early departure as a redshirt, so it is never flagged. 2. **Fifth-year class** — appearing at eligibility class 5, one year beyond the nominal four-year window. Both flags are *redshirt-shaped*, not certified, for three reasons. First, a no-stat season is not proof of non-participation: a deep-bench player can appear in games without recording a statistic, a season can end early to injury, and (pre-2018 rules) even four appearances disqualify a redshirt while still producing a thin stat line. Second, a class-5 player may be a grad transfer or junior-college arrival rather than a redshirt. Third — and most consequential here — whether a stat line exists at all depends on how completely the source records statistics, and it records them for well under half of roster seasons in the early years. The second chart below is built to make exactly that visible. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} viz_redshirt_by_career_length(flagged) ``` ::: {#fig-redshirt-career .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} viz_redshirt_seasonality(flagged) ``` ::: {#fig-redshirt-seasonality .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: The seasonality chart reads like a ledger for each season: grey is what we *know* (a stat line exists, so the player competed), teal is what the flag claims (no stats, came back), and amber is what we deliberately refuse to judge (no stats in a final season). Two things stand out. First, grey grows from about a quarter of roster seasons in 2010–2015 to around 60% by 2021 — the source did not record stats for most players in the early years at all, which is why the teal share there (45–48%) is dominated by missing data rather than redshirts. Second, even in the best-covered seasons teal runs ~25%: that is an **upper bound** on redshirting, mixing true redshirts with bench players who never recorded a statistic. The teal share only becomes meaningfully comparable *across* seasons with similar grey shares, which is roughly 2016 onward (2020's bump reflects COVID-era eligibility rules and a shortened stat season). The career-length split above should be read the same way: descriptive of the flag, never a certified redshirt rate. ## Movement — transfers College players change schools more than they used to — the transfer portal has made it routine — and *where* a player moves matters as much as *that* they move: a jump from a Group-of-Five program to a Power-Five roster is a different bet than a lateral move within the same tier. This section counts team changes by season and splits each move by **tier direction**: `up` means the move went to a higher conference tier (e.g. G5 → Power), where direction is evaluated against the season-aware tier of each school, so conference realignment is read against the season of the move rather than a fixed conference list. Hover a segment for the count. Counts come from the player-season change features (stat-line players). The career-grain rate below — computed on the full roster backbone — is the share of players whose career included **at least one** transfer; together the two views answer how common movement is, when it clusters (rule changes, portal eras), and whether it tends to be upward. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} viz_transfers_by_season(tar_read(ps_change)) ``` ::: {#fig-transfers .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
``` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rate <- transfer_rate(tar_read(career)) ``` ::: Of the 135,275 players on rosters, 18,460 (13.6%) changed teams at least once. ::: {.callout-note} Both views undercount subtly: the per-season counts only cover players with a stat line, and neither view sees a transfer whose origin season has no roster row. A gap-season move (sit out, then appear elsewhere) still counts, because the direction compares to the prior *observed* season. ::: ## Player dossier `player_dossier()` resolves a player's scattered rows into one **interpreted** record (decision 0019) rather than a raw extract that is easy to misread. Each dossier shows: identity and physicals; college statistics grouped and labeled by game **phase** (offense / defense / special teams); per-season coaching context; name-guarded high-school recruiting; the NFL outcome (drafted or undrafted-signed) with longevity; and a provenance / caveats block. Below are the **#1 overall picks of the past five NFL drafts**, each rendered as an interpreted dossier. Notes: - A bare `TD` in the long `player_stats` is ambiguous, so stats are relabelled by phase (e.g. "Passing touchdowns" vs "Defensive touchdowns"). - A blank coach cell is shown as "head coach not available" — the CFBD coaches feed is FBS head coaches only, so a non-FBS season (e.g. Cam Ward's 2021 FCS year at Incarnate Word) is flagged, not silently dropped. - Recruiting is name-guarded (decision 0013);
